title: Mr. X & The Department of Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation
text:
Decision
Mr. X & The Department of Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation
From
Office of the Information Commissioner (OIC)
Case number: OIC-200088-A0A0G2
Published on 9 July 2026
Background
Scope of Review
Preliminary Matters
My Analysis
Decision
Right of Appeal
Whether the Department was justified in refusing the applicant’s request for further records relating to a decision not to approve increases to the pensions of medical scientists who retired prior to 1 January 2024 under section 15(1)(a) of the FOI Act, on the grounds that no relevant records were found after all reasonable steps were carried out to locate them
9 July 2026
Background
In a request dated 1 September 2025 (with the agreed wording and timeline finalised on 9 September 2025), the applicant sought access to all records in relation to the Department’s decision not to approve the application of pay increases to the pensions of medical scientists who retired prior to 1 January 2024 as per the recommendation contained in the Conal Devine Medical Scientist Grades Assessment report published in January 2023. The Department interpreted the timeline of this request to be for records dating from 1 January 2023 to 3 April 2024.
It is noted that the applicant submitted a substantially similar request to the Department of Health for which a decision is also issuing by today’s date (Case number OIC-200087-A0A0G1, available on our website at
www.oic.ie
).
On 29 September 2025, the Department made a decision to grant the applicant’s request. The Department identified one record, a short email thread between the Department, the HSE, and the Department of Health from March 2024, as falling within the scope of the applicant’s request and released this in full.
On 10 October 2025, the applicant sought an internal review of the Department’s decision. The applicant said that that the email thread released by the Department did not provide him with the relevant information he was looking for. The applicant said he was seeking records showing who made and signed off on the decision not to award the increase granted under the Devine Report to medical scientists who retired prior to the 1 January 2024. The applicant said that, given that the Minister has statutory responsibility for approving pay increases to pensioners, it is inconceivable that no departmental records exist around this matter.
On 22 October 2025, the Department’s internal reviewer affirmed its original decision.
On 19 January 2026, the applicant applied to this Office for a review of the Department’s decision. In submissions to this Office dated 9 February 2026, the applicant said that the denial of the relevant increase recommended in the Conal Devine report is in breach of the Department’s guidelines on pay parity (referenced P18-13-2018) dated 24 September 2024. He said that it is also in breach of a guarantee given by the Department’s Deputy Secretary General to ICTU on 1 February 2024 that if a wage agreement was accepted the current policy of maintaining parity between pay of serving staff and pensions awarded under pre-existing public service pension schemes would be extended for the duration of the new pay agreement 2024-2026.
I have now completed my review in accordance with section 22(2) of the FOI Act. In carrying out my review, I have had regard to the submissions made by the Department and the applicant. I have decided to conclude this review by way of a formal, binding decision.
Scope of Review
The Department’s position is that no further relevant records exist or can be found within the scope of the applicant’s request. This is, in essence, a refusal to grant access to further relevant records under section 15(1)(a) of the FOI Act, which provides for the refusal of a request where the records sought do not exist or cannot be found.
Accordingly, this review is concerned solely with whether the Department was justified in refusing access, under section 15(1)(a), to further records falling within the scope of the applicant’s request.
Preliminary Matters
Before addressing the substantive matters relating to this review, I would like to address some preliminary matters.
First, it is important to note that a review by this Office is considered to be “ de novo
”, which means that in this case, it is based on the circumstances and the law as they pertain at the time of my decision and is not confined to the basis upon which the FOI body reached its decision.
Secondly, it is important to note that section 13(4) of the FOI Act provides that in deciding whether to grant or refuse a request, any reason that the requester gives for the request shall be disregarded. This means that I cannot have regard to the applicant’s motives for seeking access to the information in question, except in so far as those motives reflect what might be regarded as genuine public interest factors in favour of release of the information where the FOI Act requires a consideration of the public interest (not relevant in this case).
Thirdly, the FOI Act provides for the access to records that are actually held. It does not provide for a right of access to records which ought to exist. With one exception, which does not apply here, the FOI Act does not require FOI bodies to create a record if none exists.
Finally, it is also important to note that this Office has no remit to investigate complaints, to adjudicate on how FOI bodies perform their functions generally, or to act as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism with respect to actions taken by FOI bodies.
Analysis and Findings
Section 15(1)(a)
Section 15(1)(a) of the Act provides for the refusal of a request where the records sought do not exist or cannot be found after all reasonable steps to ascertain their whereabouts have been taken. The role of this Office in a case such as this is to review the decision of the FOI body and to decide whether that decision was justified. This means that I must have regard to the evidence available to the decision maker and to the reasoning used by the decision maker in arriving at his/her decision and also must assess the adequacy of the searches conducted by the FOI body in looking for relevant records.
Department’s submissions
In its submissions to this Office, by way of background, the Department said that
in 2023, the Labour Court recommended the implementation of the findings of the Report on Medical Scientist Grades Assessment (also known as the Devine report) no later than 1 January 2024. It said that this recommendation then formed part of the negotiations which culminated in the Public Service Pay Agreement 2024-2026. The Department further said that Circular 2/2024 set forth new rates for the Medical Scientist grades that were applied to existing staff with effect from 1 January 2024. It said this constituted a regrading and a move to a new scale for the relevant staff. It said that it is established practice that in such cases, any attendant pay increases are not passed on to those who retired before its implementation.
The Department said that it understood the applicant’s request to relate to records concerning the application of pay increases to the pensions of medical scientists who retired prior to 1 January 2024 as a result of the 2023 Labour Court recommendation. The Department said that the relevant business areas for this request were Pay and Industrial Relations and the Public Service Pensions Policy Unit. It said that the request was primarily dealt with by staff responsible for health pay and industrial relations in the Pay & Industrial Relations Unit in Public Sector Resourcing Division.
The Department said that staff in its Public Service Pensions Policy Unit of Work and Pensions Division were asked to search for any relevant records. It said that searches were conducted of staff email inboxes and folders, network shared drives, and eDocs file management system to identify relevant records. The key terms the Department said it used in the searches included: “ pensions
”, “ medical scientists
”, “ Conal
”, “ Devine
”, “ MLSA
”, “pensioners” and “award” between 1 January 2023 to 3 April 2024.
The Department further said that, where relevant, manual searches were conducted to identify if any hard copy files existed. It said that a Microsoft Excel file listing hard copy files was examined and no records relevant to the applicant’s request were identified. The Department also said it also manually searched files in the office and no hard copy records were identified.
As a result of all searches, the Department said that the only relevant record identified was the email thread it released to the applicant. It said no further records were identified to be within the remit of the request.
The Department also specifically addressed a number of queries put by the Investigating Officer assigned to this case. More particularly, the Investigating Officer had asked the Department if it holds any records showing who made and signed off on the decision not to award the increase granted under the Devine Report to medical scientists who retired prior to the 1 January 2024. In response, the Department said that no records exist of a “ decision not to award the increase granted under the Devine Report to medical scientists who retired prior to the 1 January 2024
” as an established policy exists that provided for the relevant outcome in this matter. The Department said established public service pension policy dictates that where a post is upgraded, the terms of the upgrade apply from the date of the sanctioned upgrade. The Department said that this does not apply retrospectively to previous postholders, either employees who formerly held the post or retirees who previously held the post. It said this pertains across all grades of staff across the public service. The Department provided a link to its website which outlines this policy -
https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/application-of-pay-parity-as-pension-increase-policy-in-line-with-the-public-service-a.pdf
The Investigating Officer also sought further information from the Department as to whether any meetings or discussions which took place in relation to a decision not to approve the application of pay increases to the pensions of medical scientists who retired prior to 1 January 2024 and, if so, were there any record of such meetings or discussions. In response, the Department said no record of any meetings or discussions was found during the search for records.
Finally, the Department said that it considered that the pensions referred to in the applicant’s request are likely governed by the HSE Employee Superannuation Scheme. It said that pension increases under this scheme are governed by Section 13 which states " The Executive may grant such increases in such pensions and preserved pensions under this Scheme as may be authorised from time to time by the Minister with the consent of the Minister for Finance
" (now the Minister for Health and the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation). The Department said that any adjustment to the terms and conditions, which would include pensions, of any grade of staff would require the approval of itself and the Department of Health.
Applicant’s submissions
The Investigating Officer provided the applicant with a summary of the Department’s submissions as outlined above and invited the applicant to make further submissions of his own which he duly did.
In response, the applicant said that the Department’s submissions referred to regrading/upgrading which he said is the first mention of this and was not part of the terms of reference of the Devine Report. The applicant said there has been no prior mention of regrading/upgrading in any of the documents released by the Department. The applicant said that as different rules regarding pensions apply to special pay awards and upgrade/regrade, the classification of the increases under the Devine Report is fundamental to his FOI request. He said that it is inconceivable that a decision of this importance has not been documented and apparently no records of it exist in the Department.
My Analysis
It is important to note that the FOI Act does not require absolute certainty as to the existence or location of records, as situations can arise where records are lost or simply cannot be found. What the FOI Act requires is that the public body concerned takes all reasonable steps to locate relevant records. Furthermore, it is open to this Office to find that an FOI body has satisfied the requirements of section 15(1)(a), even where records that an applicant believes ought to exist, or are known to have existed in the past, have not been located. We do not generally expect FOI bodies to carry out extensive or indefinite general searches for records simply because an applicant asserts that records sought ought to exist or did exist.
The question I must consider, therefore, is whether the Department has taken all reasonable steps to ascertain the whereabouts of the specific records sought.
The Department’s position is that having carried out searches, no records, beyond the email thread already released to the applicant, within the scope of the request exist or can be found. The applicant is not satisfied that all relevant records have been identified and released.
Having carefully considered the Department’s submissions in this matter, I am satisfied that it has provided a sufficiently detailed and cogent explanation as to why no further records exist. In particular, I am satisfied that the Department has carried out all reasonable steps to search for records relevant to the applicant’s request. I am further satisfied that the Department’s explanation of an established policy whereby public service post regrades/upgrades do not apply retrospectively to previous postholders, whether it be employees who formerly held the post, or retirees who previously held the post, adequately explains why no formal decision was taken by the Department as referred to in the applicant’s request. While I acknowledge the applicant’s arguments in his application and submissions that relevant records ought to exist, in the absence of any evidence to suggest that further searches are warranted in this case, I am satisfied that the Department has carried out all reasonable steps to search for and provide the relevant records which are within the scope of the applicant’s request.
Accordingly, I find that the Department was justified in refusing access to records within the scope of the request under section 15(1)(a) of the Act on the basis that the records do not exist or cannot be found after all reasonable steps to ascertain their whereabouts have been taken.
Decision
Having carried out a review under section 22(2) of the FOI Act, I hereby affirm the Department’s decision to refuse the release of further records within the scope of applicant’s request under section 15(1)(a), on the grounds that the Department carried out all reasonable steps to locate all relevant records.
Right of Appeal
Section 24 of the FOI Act sets out detailed provisions for an appeal to the High Court by a party to a review, or any other person affected by the decision. In summary, such an appeal, normally on a point of law, must be initiated not later than four weeks after notice of the decision was given to the person bringing the appeal.

Mary Connery
Investigator
respondent: The Department of Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation
